claims.statement: Entering find mode triggers exactly one nearby search at the current map center, and panning or zooming the map never issues a request; the only re-search entry point is the explicit `이 위치 다시 찾기` button, which calls `search()` against the latest center held in `centerRef`.

The hook's effect keyed only on `mode` bumps `requestRef` (invalidating any response still in flight), clears both candidate arrays, both pending selection arrays, `loading`, and `error`, and issues a request only when `mode !== null` — so exiting the search runs the same reset with no request and a late response from a cancelled search is dropped rather than resurrecting candidates.

`useInlineMapSearch` mirrors `mode`, `center`, `savedStops`, and `savedStations` into refs updated during render so that `search` is a stable `useCallback` with an empty dependency array yet still reads fresh values at call time — this is what makes a center change a ref write with no fetch triggered by re-render.

Every state write inside `search()` is guarded by `requestRef.current === request`, including the `finally` block that clears `loading`, so a superseded response commits nothing and cannot unset the loading flag of the request that replaced it.

A saved stop or station never appears as its own candidate: the hook filters fetched results against the saved ids read from `savedStopsRef`/`savedStationsRef` at call time, and `MapCanvas` independently filters the pending arrays again against ids derived from its saved marker props, so the invariant survives removal of either filter.
A bus search sets `busStops` and clears `stations` to `[]`, and a subway search does the converse, so the two modes can never both hold live candidates at once.

An empty candidate list after filtering is surfaced through the same `error` slot a transport failure uses (`이 주변에서 새 정류장을 찾지 못했습니다.` / `이 주변에서 새 지하철역을 찾지 못했습니다.`), so an empty result and a failed request are indistinguishable to the status paragraph — deliberately, because the remedy of panning and re-searching is the same.

Search failures map to mode-specific Korean retry sentences, except an `ApiError` with `code === "INVALID_LOCATION"` (detected by `isServiceAreaError`), which maps to `서울 서비스 범위 밖이에요. 지도를 서울 근처로 옮겨 주세요.` — the one failure that tells the user to move the map rather than retry.

The finder renders as an overlay on the same `MapContainer` at the same center with saved markers still drawn — there is no dialog, scrim, or second map instance; this is pinned by `MapStage.test.tsx` and `App.test.tsx` asserting `queryByRole("dialog")` is absent.

Finder state is split across three owners with disjoint lifetimes: `App` holds `searchMode` (whether and which mode is being searched), `MapStage` holds the working `mapCenter` fed by `MapCanvas`'s `onCenterChange`, and `useInlineMapSearch` holds candidates and pending selection — created and torn down with the search and never persisted.

The `정류장 찾기`/`역 찾기` trigger carries `id="point-search-trigger"`, `aria-pressed`, and a label that flips to `찾기 취소` while active; its handler is a toggle (`current === mode ? null : mode`), and `App.closeSearch()` clears `searchMode` then refocuses `#point-search-trigger` inside a `queueMicrotask` so keyboard users land back on the opening button.

Four distinct user actions cancel an in-flight search — the trigger a second time, the overlay's `취소`, switching the `출근`/`퇴근` commute context, and switching the `버스`/`지하철` mode tab — and all four are pure `setSearchMode(null)` with no additional cleanup, because the hook's own entry effect performs the reset.

On a phone with the map closed, entering a search mounts the map, because `App` renders `MapStage` whenever `isDesktop || mobileMapOpen || searchMode !== null`; the stage is `flex: 0 0 55dvh; height: 55dvh` below 960px, and `MapStage` hides its `지도 닫기` button while searching so the only exits from the finder are cancel, save, or the trigger.

The candidate marker and the candidate list row expose the identical `aria-pressed` for the same candidate, because both derive it from the same pending-selection array: `MapStage` merges pending selected ids into `selectedStopIds`/`selectedSubwayStationIds` for `MapCanvas` and passes the same arrays as `selectedBusStopIds`/`selectedStationIds` to the reel — toggling from either surface flips both, and neither surface is privileged.

Saved markers keep rendering through a search while candidates render as dashed markers — `map-marker-pending` uses `stroke-dasharray: 5 3` on `--route-blue` and `map-marker-pending-subway` on `--subway`, and the `is-active` variant drops the dash, switches stroke to `--ink`, and fills with the lime `--signal`, so selection is carried by stroke geometry plus `aria-pressed`, never by color alone.

CircleMarker elements are upgraded to buttons by an effect keyed on `[label, active]` that sets `role="button"`, `tabindex="0"`, `aria-label`, a live `aria-pressed`, and the `map-marker-hit-target` class — this shape is required because react-leaflet exposes the Leaflet instance through a ref and Leaflet's `add` event fires once, so attaching attributes in a one-shot event callback would freeze `aria-pressed` at its first-render value and selection changes would never reach the DOM.

On `Enter` or `Space` the marker's keydown handler calls `preventDefault()`, then `marker.closePopup()` before invoking the select callback and `marker.openPopup()` — the pre-close is required so the newly opened popup replaces any popup that was already open, matching Leaflet's click behavior instead of stacking or suppressing it; `Escape` closes the popup without selecting.

The `onSelect` callback is stored in a ref updated during render (`onSelectRef.current = onSelect`) so the keydown listener, which is detached and re-attached on every `[label, active]` run, always invokes the current toggle rather than a closure captured at listener-attachment time.

Each map point is two `CircleMarker`s: a visible `radius={9}` circle marked `interactive: false` and a dedicated invisible `radius={22}` (44px-diameter) hit circle carrying click, keyboard, and all ARIA state — the hit area is real SVG geometry rather than a CSS box, and because the visible circle is non-interactive Leaflet never adds `.leaflet-interactive` to it, which is why the token CSS rules style the marker class names directly instead of gating on Leaflet's class.

`is-active` is toggled on the visible marker's element through an effect (`classList.add(baseClass)` plus `classList.toggle("is-active", …)`) because Leaflet applies `pathOptions.className` only at creation and `setStyle` never re-applies it — toggling the class through props alone would be a no-op after first render.

Leaflet's `popupopen`/`popupclose` are re-dispatched as bubbling DOM custom events carrying the popup instance and its `_source` marker link, so a frame-level `Escape` handler can close whichever popup is open and restore focus to the owning marker element — but only when `document.activeElement` was inside the popup content, leaving marker-focused and container-focused Escape to keep their natural target.

`InlineMapSearchControls` is a focusable `<section tabIndex={-1}>` labeled `버스 정류장 지도 찾기`/`지하철역 지도 찾기` that takes focus on mount; its `저장` button is labeled `{selectedCount}곳 저장` and `disabled` until at least one candidate is picked, and its status paragraph is a polite single-sentence `aria-live` region (`지도 중심 주변을 찾는 중…`, the error string, or `가까운 {정류장|역} {resultCount}곳`) that never re-reads the list.

Candidates render into a `<fieldset className="inline-map-result-reel">` with an sr-only legend, laid out as one horizontal scroll lane (`overflow-x: auto`, `scroll-snap-type: inline proximity`, `min-inline-size: 0`) pinned to the bottom of the map — satisfying the mobile contract of a single-line scroll area with no second vertical scroll surface; below the 960px breakpoint the toolbar and status stack vertically and the two action buttons become a two-column grid.

`저장` branches on `searchMode` in `MapStage` and hands the pending array to `App`, which commits through `addBusStops(commute, stops)`/`addSubwayStations(commute, stations)` (the single `useTransitSelections` mutator that writes localStorage or enqueues `PUT /api/settings`), sets a polite announcement, forces `mode` to match what was saved, and calls `closeSearch()` — nothing reaches the selections document before this point.

`취소` discards only the candidates: it runs `closeSearch()` and nothing else, so the saved document is untouched (no mutator call, no storage write, no `PUT /api/settings`), the working map center stays exactly where the user panned it (`MapStage`'s `mapCenter` is only reset by the effect on the `center` prop, which a cancel does not change), and `mode`/`commute` are preserved — unlike save, which forces `mode`.

Product caps are applied at commit time, not at pick time: `addBusStopsToCommute` appends every candidate to the unbounded saved list but unions ids into `selectedBusStopIds` sliced to `MAX_SELECTED_BUS_STOPS` (= 4), while `addSubwayStationsToCommute` sets `selectedSubwayStationId` to `stations[0]` because subway is single-watch — so the pending selection itself is unbounded inside the search.

Saving deliberately moves the map while cancelling does not: a save changes the selections and therefore `App`'s derived `mapAnchor`, which flows down as the `center` prop and makes `CenterObserver` call `map.setView(center, zoom, {animate: false})` when the centers differ by more than 0.0001 degrees — an unanimated snap to the first saved point that serves as a confirmation cue.

`MapCanvas`'s `CenterObserver` reports Leaflet `moveend` centers to `MapStage` only after coalescing them through `requestAnimationFrame` (skipping changes below 1e-7 degrees), and also writes the resolved center and Leaflet animation options into the container's `dataset` as machine-consumable QA truth — so a fast drag produces one center update per frame rather than one per event.

The two nearby fetchers differ in both default radius and timeout: `fetchNearbyStops(center, radius = 800)` uses the client's default 8-second abort, while `fetchNearbySubwayStations(center, radius = 3_000)` requests a 35-second abort because a cold subway catalog must first load the quarterly official T-Data CSV server-side — both Zod-parse the response body and throw a structured `ApiError(status, code)` on any non-2xx.

`GET /api/stops/nearby` and `GET /api/subway/nearby` safeParse the raw query with `nearbySearchSchema`/`subwaySearchSchema` and throw `400 INVALID_LOCATION` on failure, and wrap catalog failures in `502 UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE` with an upstream detail — the `INVALID_LOCATION` code is what the client's `isServiceAreaError` translates into the move-the-map sentence.

The Leaflet drag clamp is deliberately padded beyond the API's validation window: `MapCanvas`'s `maxBounds` is `[[37.2, 126.6], [37.95, 127.45]]` with `maxBoundsViscosity: 1.0`, while both schemas accept only lat 37.3–37.8 and lng 126.7–127.3 — so a user can drag to a corner the API refuses, and that refusal is exactly the case the service-area sentence exists to explain.

The nearby endpoints do not ask Seoul what is nearby: `TransitCatalogService.nearbyStops` maps every in-memory catalog point through haversine distance, filters to within the requested radius, sorts by distance then id, and rounds the distance; `nearbySubway` additionally dedupes by station name keeping the closest point per name, so a multi-line transfer station collapses to one candidate.

The bus nearby path has a live-upstream fallback the subway path lacks: if the bus catalog read throws an `UpstreamError` (catalog rejected or never loaded), the service falls back to `fetchLiveNearbyStops`, a location-scoped query against Seoul's `selectNearStops.do` — the only place the nearby path hits Seoul per request, and the sequence of a rejected 45 km catalog load followed by a `kiloMeter=0.8` live query is pinned by an e2e test.

`locate.ts`'s header comment records a deliberate negative result: the platform's accuracy radius is not a reliable rejection signal, because a fix can be centered exactly right while reporting a conservative multi-kilometer radius (IP-based fallback does this constantly) and rejecting on radius broke locate entirely — so coarse fixes are accepted and flagged, the map still pans, and the caller shows a soft notice.

`requestCurrentPosition()` returns a discriminated `LocateResult` (`located` with lat, lng, accuracy, and coarse; `unsupported` when `navigator.geolocation` is absent; `unavailable` on the error callback) and flags a fix coarse when its accuracy is non-finite or above `COARSE_LOCATE_ACCURACY_METERS = 200`, while never rejecting it.

Fixes at or above `IP_FALLBACK_ACCURACY_METERS = 3_000` are treated as almost certainly IP-based fallback where the center is the ISP's registered area rather than the user, so `locateCoarseNotice` returns a notice pointing at device settings and location permissions — explicitly not at a retry, because no app-side retry can improve it; coarse-but-closer fixes instead get a notice stating the error distance and asking the user to drag the map if it is not their location, since the map already moved.

The geolocation call passes `enableHighAccuracy: true`, `timeout: 8_000`, and `maximumAge: 0`, the last forbidding cached fixes outright — a cached fix can be where the user was a minute ago, not where they are now.

`locate.ts` currently has no callers in the web tree and the `.locate-button` CSS is equally dormant (a leftover of the dialog-based picker the inline finder replaced), so the geolocation boundary is implemented and documented but not wired into the UI.
